competitions.name: First Proof
competitions.tagline: Unpublished research-level math problems; AI systems get one shot each and expert referees grade the proofs blind.
competitions.description: First Proof is an independent benchmark run by research mathematicians to measure whether AI systems can autonomously prove research-level results. Each batch collects problems that arose in the contributors' own work and whose proofs are unpublished; the editorial board runs every system itself, one shot per problem with no human input, and expert referees grade the proofs double blind. Batch 2 (2026-06-10): 4 systems, 39 graded solutions, 7 of 10 problems got at least one passing proof; P4, P8, P10 remain open. Batch 3 is under way; results are due 2026-10-14.

participation.howToSubmit: Systems enter per batch through the call for submissions on 1stproof.org (Batch 3 applications closed 2026-09-10). A system is an open-source harness calling publicly available models, or a public product; First Proof clones the submitter's repository, builds its Docker image on an approved EC2 instance and runs it once on the problem file, following the protocol published with each batch (e.g. 1stproof/batch-2).
participation.submissionFormat: A repository with Dockerfile, hardware.json, README.md and src/; the container reads the LaTeX problems from /data/input/input.json and writes LaTeX proofs to /data/output.
participation.computeDetails: Runs on First Proof's AWS instances; model API usage goes on the submitter's keys. Batch 2 systems spent $117–$4,799 in API fees for 10 problems.
participation.rounds: Batches of unpublished research problems, each graded and published with every solution and referee report, plus community experiments where problems are posted publicly and solutions follow a week later.
participation.eligibility: AI companies and academic teams; only publicly available models, or harnesses that will be released.
participation.cost: free to enter; API usage is paid by the submitter
participation.verification: Each proof is refereed double blind by at least two experts in the field; the editorial board decides essentially flawless, minor revisions, major revisions or reject. Problems, human solutions, AI solutions, referee reports and logs are all published.
requirements: Open-source harness or public AI product

competitions.name: LeanEval
competitions.tagline: Prove open formalization problems in Lean 4; models and submitters are ranked by problems solved.
competitions.description: LeanEval is the Lean FRO's comparator-based benchmark for formal mathematics. Trusted theorem statements live in leanprover/lean-eval; a problem counts as solved when the comparator accepts a submitted proof. Results are sticky per (user, model, problem) and published at lean-lang.org/eval. 304 visible problems, 75 models, 60 submitters, 39 active problems still unsolved.

participation.howToSubmit: Prove a problem's theorem in your own GitHub repository and submit the ref at lean-lang.org/eval/submit; the comparator verifies the proof and the result is appended to results/<login>.json in leanprover/lean-eval-submissions.
participation.submissionFormat: GitHub repo + ref containing the completed Lean proof, plus the declared model label used to produce it.
participation.computeDetails: Scoring is a comparator check of the proof; whatever compute the prover needs is on the submitter's side.
participation.eligibility: Open to everyone. Successes are sticky: an accepted (user, model, problem) tuple is never removed.
participation.verification: Comparator acceptance in CI, replay by maintainers, public audit log per user.

git clone https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval && cd lean-eval
